scope: Independent read-only preparation source review; no private cases, application execution, build or gates.

findings.evidence: verify.json initially invoked python3 without -B. stress_cli.py imports test_cli, creating __pycache__ in a fresh source tree, which project.py would detect as changed project identity.
findings.resolution: Both commands now use /usr/bin/python3 -B; no runtime acceptance result claimed by this source review.

observations.assessment: Every Job field receives a value in the initialized buffer and again when a validated job maps to its sorted unique ID. Finish-only update preserves duration and dependency tape node. Grouped borrows use distinct owned buffers, remain synchronous, and no reference is returned.
Sort and lower_bound use the same decoded-JSON-string comparator. Lookup checks equality after a bounded lower bound; escaped equivalent IDs match and empty prefixes cannot be indexed.

Exact object cardinalities plus all required fields reject missing and unknown keys. Typed integer bounds reject null, bool and floating values. Complete schema validation precedes duplicate IDs, repeated dependency IDs, unknown IDs, then cycle handling. Dependency objects remain invalid in v1.

Cycle removal preserves downstream blocked jobs; emitted identifiers are sorted. Lexicographic first-ready order and snapshot-before-completion layers remain distinct. Scratch covers 128 dependencies and 16384 unknown occurrences; empty graph emits empty collections and zero makespan. Maximum valid duration chain is safely within i64.
Exact original std_text::read(heap, 1048576) mutation site and parser budget are preserved. No dependency lags, priority, slack or cycle-group features are introduced.

Original assertions remain. Added cursor-schema cases cover missing/null/wrong kinds, extra field replacement and schema precedence. Stress now fails on timeouts/nonzero exits and compares entire dense-cycle blocked and 16384-unknown outputs.

limits: Source review of stable but uncommitted planner edits, pinned by hashes; later source changes require re-review.
No execution, allocation-failure or integrated compiler proof from this review. Compiler borrow/callback semantics were reviewed separately in callback-review.json.

cache_retention_review.assessment: Opt-in is configuration-frozen and omitted when false. Each command gets a new event-numbered directory under the coordinator lock and its own fresh cache mounted by isolation.run; no cross-command cache reuse. Result includes a bounded directory digest or explicit cache_retention_error before normal output/status and result hash recording. Phase deadline checks still include post-command processing.
cache_retention_review.test_evidence: test_opt_in_retains_each_command_cache_without_cross_command_reuse creates two reports, asserts each starts absent, retains both distinct values and receipt fields, and rejects changing the configuration. Reviewed source only.
limits: Unsafe, special-file or over-budget cache trees cannot receive a retained_cache digest; explicit retention error is the documented observable limit, not proof of a complete hashed cache.
Retention adds hashing time to command phase accounting; no timing measurements reviewed.
